creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`devenv/devenv` names one image, one container and one port as constants
(`IMAGE=muster-devenv`, `CONTAINER=muster-devenv`, `PORT=2222`, lines 20-22), but
takes its ssh key from `$REPO_ROOT/devenv/.ssh/id_ed25519` (line 23), which is a
different path in every worktree. `up` generates the key if it is missing (line 49)
and `docker build` bakes it into the image (line 55).

So `./devenv/devenv up` from a second worktree rebuilds the shared image around that
worktree's key. The first worktree's `--ssh` and `--corpus-linux` runs then fail to
authenticate against a container that is up and healthy, and nothing on either side
says the image was rebuilt underneath them.

## How it was found

A parallel-work round put three agents in `muster-1`, `muster-2` and `muster-3`.
Slot 1 (`crates/muster-ssh`) needed the remote tier and slot 2 needed
`--corpus-linux`; slot 2 read the script and raised the collision before either
started a container. Both tiers were serialized by hand instead, which is the
workaround: one worktree holds docker at a time, and the others wait.

That workaround costs more than the wait. Slot 2's patch adds `python3` to
`devenv/Dockerfile`, so the two slots also disagree about what the image should
contain, and whoever builds first builds the wrong one.

## Two directions

Derive the image, container and port from the worktree, so each gets its own. Every
worktree can then run its tier whenever it likes, at the cost of a container per
worktree - and `./dev --doctor`, which reports the devenv container today, would have
to report several.

Or keep one container and stop the key being per-worktree - generate it once outside
the repo, or take it from a fixed path. Cheaper, and it removes the silent lockout,
but the tiers still have to take turns and a Dockerfile change in one worktree still
reaches the others.

Worth deciding which, rather than leaving the serialization as folklore that each
round rediscovers.
title: 🐳 Two worktrees cannot both run the devenv tier, and the loser fails on a key
